name: Agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia
aliases: Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (agitation)
summary: Two drugs are FDA-labeled for agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease: brexpiprazole (2023, an antipsychotic with the dementia-mortality boxed warning) and dextromethorphan-bupropion (approved April 2026, the first non-antipsychotic for this indication). Neither is indicated for as-needed (prn) use; nonpharmacologic approaches and evaluation for medical causes come first.
plainSummary: Many people with Alzheimer's disease become restless, irritable, or aggressive. Two prescription medicines are approved to help with this, and doctors usually try non-drug approaches and look for other causes such as pain or infection first.

approved.indication: Treatment of agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease. Not indicated as an as-needed ("prn") treatment for this agitation.

dosing.target: 1 mg once daily on days 8–14, then 2 mg once daily from day 15
dosing.max: 3 mg once daily (after at least 14 days at 2 mg, based on response and tolerability)
dosing.notes: CYP2D6 poor metabolizers: half the usual dose (quarter dose if also taking a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor). Moderate–severe hepatic impairment or CrCl <60 mL/min: max 2 mg once daily.

boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (antidepressant class warning)
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to brexpiprazole or any component
approved.plainSummary: Brexpiprazole is a daily pill that can reduce agitation in people with Alzheimer's dementia. Like other antipsychotics, it carries a warning about a higher risk of death in older adults with dementia.

verified.note: Checked on the Rexulti label (revised 4/2026). A generic brexpiprazole label (Ajanta, ANDA) exists on DailyMed but lists only MDD and schizophrenia, so no generic carries this indication; genericAvailable is false for this indication.

approved.drugClass: NMDA receptor antagonist / sigma-1 agonist + aminoketone (norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor; CYP2D6 inhibitor)
approved.indication: Treatment of agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease. Not indicated as an as-needed ("prn") treatment for this agitation.

dosing.start: 30 mg/105 mg once daily in the morning
dosing.target: Day 8: 30 mg/105 mg twice daily (at least 8 hours apart); day 15: 45 mg/105 mg twice daily
dosing.max: 45 mg/105 mg twice daily (no more than 2 doses per day)
dosing.notes: Known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30–59): start 30 mg/105 mg once daily, max 45 mg/105 mg once daily from day 8. Not recommended in severe renal (eGFR 15–29) or severe hepatic impairment.

formulations: Extended-release tablets 30 mg/105 mg and 45 mg/105 mg (dextromethorphan HBr/bupropion HCl)
boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (antidepressant class warning)
contraindications: Current or prior diagnosis of bulimia or anorexia nervosa
Abrupt discontinuation of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, or antiepileptic drugs
Taking, or within 14 days of stopping, MAOIs
Known hypersensitivity to bupropion, dextromethorphan, or other components
approved.plainSummary: Auvelity is a pill taken once or twice a day that can lower agitation in people with Alzheimer's dementia, and it is not an antipsychotic. It should not be used by people who have seizures.

verified.note: Indication, dosing (including the new 45 mg/105 mg strength), contraindications, and boxed warning checked on the label (revised 8/2026). Approval date (April 30, 2026) is from trade press (AJMC, Healio); the label shows only 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2022'.
